theory.intro: To compare lengths fairly, first write them in the **same unit**. Then the numbers can be compared directly.
facts: You cannot compare $1.2$ m and $90$ cm until both use one unit.
Useful links: $1$ m $= 100$ cm, $1$ cm $= 10$ mm, $1$ km $= 1000$ m.
Convert to the **smaller** unit to avoid decimals, or to a common unit of your choice.
steps: Choose one common unit for all the lengths.
Convert every length into that unit.

foundation.question_text: Which is longer: a $1.4$ m skipping rope or a $135$ cm skipping rope?
foundation.solution_text:
$1.4\text{ m}=140\text{ cm}$
$140\text{ cm}>135\text{ cm}$
The $1.4$ m rope is longer.

foundation.question_text: Are $2.5$ m and $250$ cm equal in length?
foundation.solution_text:
$2.5\text{ m}=250\text{ cm}$
The lengths are equal.

foundation.question_text: Order these walking routes from shortest to longest: $0.8$ km, $750$ m, $1$ km.
foundation.solution_text:
$0.8\text{ km}=800\text{ m}$
$1\text{ km}=1000\text{ m}$
$750\text{ m},\ 0.8\text{ km},\ 1\text{ km}$

foundation.question_text: Which plant is tallest: $42$ cm, $390$ mm or $0.4$ m?
foundation.solution_text:
$390\text{ mm}=39\text{ cm}$
$0.4\text{ m}=40\text{ cm}$
$42\text{ cm}>40\text{ cm}>39\text{ cm}$
The $42$ cm plant is tallest.

foundation.question_text: Which ribbon is shortest: $3.2$ m, $315$ cm or $3300$ mm?
foundation.solution_text:
$3.2\text{ m}=320\text{ cm}$
$3300\text{ mm}=330\text{ cm}$
$315\text{ cm}<320\text{ cm}<330\text{ cm}$
The $315$ cm ribbon is shortest.

development.question_text: Which shelf is longer: $1.05$ m or $104$ cm?
development.solution_text:
$1.05\text{ m}=105\text{ cm}$
$105\text{ cm}>104\text{ cm}$
The $1.05$ m shelf is longer.

development.question_text: Order these model tracks from shortest to longest: $950$ mm, $1.02$ m, $97$ cm.
development.solution_text:
$1.02\text{ m}=1020\text{ mm}$
$97\text{ cm}=970\text{ mm}$
$950\text{ mm},\ 97\text{ cm},\ 1.02\text{ m}$

development.question_text: Which two measurements are equal: $0.65$ m, $650$ mm and $65$ mm?
development.solution_text:
$0.65\text{ m}=650\text{ mm}$
The equal pair is $0.65$ m and $650$ mm.

development.question_text:
Kai says $0.99$ km is farther than $995$ m. Is Kai correct?
Explain.
development.solution_text:
$0.99\text{ km}=990\text{ m}$
$990\text{ m}<995\text{ m}$
Kai is not correct.

development.question_text: Which cable is shortest: $0.72$ m, $71$ cm or $705$ mm?
development.solution_text:
$0.72\text{ m}=720\text{ mm}$
$71\text{ cm}=710\text{ mm}$
$705\text{ mm}<710\text{ mm}<720\text{ mm}$
The $705$ mm cable is shortest.

mastery.question_text: Order these four race stages from shortest to longest: $1.2$ km, $1180$ m, $1$ km $190$ m and $1.205$ km.
mastery.solution_text:
$1.2\text{ km}=1200\text{ m}$
$1\text{ km }190\text{ m}=1190\text{ m}$
$1.205\text{ km}=1205\text{ m}$
$1180\text{ m},\ 1\text{ km }190\text{ m},\ 1.2\text{ km},\ 1.205\text{ km}$

mastery.question_text:
Sienna claims $0.099$ km is longer than $100$ m because $99>100$ is nearly true.
Correct her comparison and identify the place-value issue.
mastery.solution_text:
$0.099\text{ km}=99\text{ m}$
$99\text{ m}<100\text{ m}$
Sienna compared digits before converting to a common unit.

mastery.question_text: Which of these beams are longer than $2$ m: $199$ cm, $2050$ mm, $2.01$ m and $0.002$ km?
mastery.solution_text:
$199\text{ cm}=1.99\text{ m}$
$2050\text{ mm}=2.05\text{ m}$
$0.002\text{ km}=2\text{ m}$
The $2050$ mm and $2.01$ m beams are longer than $2$ m.
